About & How to Play

THE WAKING DEPTH is a short, complete, parser-driven interactive fiction — the kind of game you play by typing what you want to do. It runs entirely in your browser, in a terminal we built to feel like the half-dead console of a coastal lighthouse at three in the morning. No accounts, no downloads, no leaving the room. Just you, a prompt, and the dark.

How to play

You move through the lighthouse by typing simple instructions. The parser understands plain verb-and-noun commands and a generous pile of synonyms. You don't have to guess fancy phrasing — TAKE CROWBAR, GO NORTH, READ JOURNAL, and USE OILCAN ON LAMP all do exactly what they say.

  • Stuck? Type LOOK to re-read the room, or EXAMINE anything that catches your eye.
  • Type INVENTORY (or just I) to see what you're carrying.
  • Type SCORE for a live checklist of your objectives.
  • Press ↑ / ↓ in the prompt to scroll through commands you've already typed.
  • The game autosaves every move. You can also SAVE, LOAD, and RESTART from the buttons above the screen or by typing those words.

Accessibility. If your system requests reduced motion, the CRT scanlines, power-on flicker, and typewriter reveal all switch off automatically — the full text appears at once and the cursor stops blinking. The whole game is keyboard-operable and the transcript is announced to screen readers.

Command reference

LOOK · LDescribe your surroundings again.
EXAMINE · X · INSPECTLook closely at a thing or feature.
READRead text on books, journals, charts.
TAKE · GET · GRABPick something up. TAKE ALL grabs everything loose.
DROPPut something down.
INVENTORY · IList what you're carrying.
N S E W · UP · DOWN · GOMove. Bare directions work too.
OPEN · CLOSEOpen or close containers.
UNLOCKUnlock something with a key you hold.
PRY · FORCELever something open with a tool.
USE <a> ON <b>Combine or apply items. FILL, FIT, POUR, TURN map here too.
LIGHT · STRIKESet a flame to something flammable.
MAPRefresh the explored-rooms map in the side panel.
SCOREShow score, moves, and the objective checklist.
SAVE · LOAD · RESTARTManage your game (stored in this browser).
HELP · ?Show the in-game command list.

The studio

Saltwire Interactive is a two-person interactive-fiction studio working out of a converted net-loft in Cape Wrack, Nova Scotia. We make small, strange, hand-written games about the coast — about fog, debt, drowned chapels, radio static, and the particular loneliness of keeping a light burning for people you will never meet. We write everything by hand in a parser engine we maintain ourselves; no procedural text, no asset store, no filler. If a sentence is in one of our games, somebody at the kitchen table chose every word of it.

  • Maren Holloway — writing & design. Former marine archivist; once spent a season cataloguing a lighthouse's logbooks and never quite came back from it.
  • Idris Quay — engine & systems. Builds the parser, the world model, and the CRT we trap you inside. Believes a good error message is a line of dialogue.

Other works

  • The Fog Tax (2024) — a debt-collector walks a coast that keeps rearranging itself behind him.
  • Static at the Net-Loft (2025) — a numbers-station mystery told entirely through a tuning dial.
  • THE WAKING DEPTH (2026) — this one. Our shortest and, we think, our meanest.

Hints & the solution

THE WAKING DEPTH is fully winnable and fairly clued — your grandmother's journal and tide chart, both upstairs, tell you almost everything you need. But if the lamp won't wake and the night is wearing thin, the answers are below.

Gentle hints (tap to reveal)
  • You can't get into the lighthouse the polite way. The boards over the door want leverage — and there's iron in the boathouse.
  • The biscuit tin in the kitchen rattles. Open it.
  • The cabinet in the watch room needs a small brass key. Read the journal to learn where it was hidden.
  • The lamp wants three things in order: fuel, a working regulator, and a flame. You'll find all three before you climb to the top.
  • The safe combination is the year the lamp was first lit. It's written in two places upstairs.
Full winning walkthrough (heavy spoilers)
  1. west
  2. take all (crowbar, rope, oil can)
  3. east
  4. north (shore path)
  5. north (lighthouse door)
  6. pry door
  7. north (into the foyer)
  8. west (kitchen)
  9. take matches
  10. open tin
  11. take key
  12. east (back to foyer)
  13. up (keeper's quarters)
  14. read journal (learn where the key was, and the cabinet)
  15. read chart (learn the year: 1891)
  16. up (watch room)
  17. unlock cabinet (brass key — reveals logbook + valve handle)
  18. take valve handle
  19. up (lamp room)
  20. use oilcan on lamp
  21. use valve handle on lamp
  22. light lamp — THE LAMP IS LIT. You win.
